SNOMED lacks a malaria-area concept, but (snomed_concept "History of travel with high risk of exposure to communicable disease" "situation") or (snomed_concept "Travel abroad" "finding") would allow a possible (snomed_concept "Malaria" "disorder") rule, and the gap should at least be recorded.

rule_level_problems.problem: Footnote 1 defines 'shock likely' (SBP < 80, pulse >= 100, RR > 30, confusion/restlessness, weakness) and the red box cites it as 'Shock1'. No probable Shock rule exists, so the Urgent evaluation's Shock branch only fires when the nurse records (clinical_finding Shock) directly; of the footnote's components only SBP < 80 is independently in the priority rule.

'If fingerprick glucose < 3 (< 4 if diabetes) or >= 11.1 -> 19' inside the red box is a numeric criterion on a routine vital, and none of the three thresholds appears anywhere in the file. Defensible only if page 19's rules are relied on.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable acute viral infection from fever page
rule_level_problems.problem: The page reaches this box only after 'If none of the above' (no urgent signs, no AHR, no mpox or diphtheria criteria) and after the tick-bite No branch. The rule excludes tick bite but not the urgent, mpox or diphtheria findings, so a febrile patient with neck stiffness and headache gets both probable Meningitis and probable Acute viral disease. Low because the probable Meningitis rule and Urgent evaluation still fire.

'If on abacavir, check for abacavir hypersensitivity reaction' has no rule. (snomed_concept "Hypersensitivity to abacavir" "finding") exists; whether 'on abacavir' is expressible is unclear, and the line routes to page 131, so this may be cross-reference only.

The page's fever definition includes 'temperature >= 38°C ... in the past 3 days'; the trigger only uses a current measurement >= 38 or a recorded Fever complaint. The time window could be expressed with onset/time_ago but is not. Minor because (active_condition Fever) covers the common case.

rule_level_problems.rule: Check for causes of fever not needing urgent attention
rule_level_problems.problem: The tick-bite question tells the nurse to look for a 'small dark brown/black scab' (eschar). Eschar is not checked for, so a nurse who records the eschar rather than 'Tick bite' will not reach probable tick bite fever.

summary: The red box is fully and correctly encoded (all ten criteria, the two 'likely' diagnoses as probable rules referenced from the Urgent evaluation), and the mpox, diphtheria, tick bite fever and acute viral infection logic match the page; every check_for item is consumed and all 48 SNOMED concepts exist. The most consequential miss is the page's first instruction, 'consider malaria if in a malaria area in the past 3 months', which has no rule at all. Secondary gaps: footnote 1's 'shock likely' definition is not a probable Shock rule, and the red-box fingerprick-glucose thresholds (< 3, < 4 if diabetic, >= 11.1) are not encoded anywhere.
